analysis.title: Hyperscalers Rip, Semis Rot In One Of The Widest Splits In A Decade
key_insights: On Wednesday Nov 4, after the election, the Nasdaq beat the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) by nearly 460bps. Goldman's Peter Callahan calls it a top-10 daily spread in 10+ years. Apple, Amazon and Microsoft led, while semis fell further below their 200-day moving averages.

Goldman's trading desk describes a clear rotation into hyperscalers, with semis used as a source of funds. The stated logic is that a data center build freeze makes existing compute scarcer and pricier, and lower capex could free cash for buybacks.

The article says Democratic wins could freeze up to 45% of planned US data center capacity. Texas, Georgia and Michigan are named as places where new projects could be frozen. The author argues 2027 chip orders tied to those projects would slip first.

Goldman IG credit trader Kevin Boova sees big supply/demand imbalances in compute that favor infrastructure already in place. Hyperscaler CDS tightened while data center CDS widened to fresh 2026 highs.

Wells Fargo cites compute pricing data supporting the scarcity argument: H100 rental rates +26% y/y, GB200 rental pricing +50% YTD (+12% in the last month), and Oracle at 97.9% AI infrastructure utilization with a 20% average renewal/resale premium.

The buyback leg of the thesis is questioned by the author. Hyperscalers burned $31B of free cash flow in Q3 and Microsoft raised a $25B bond the morning after its earnings beat, so they would have to stop borrowing before buying back stock.

Semiconductor forward multiples compressed more than 40% in two months, from 28x to 16x. The SOX now trades at about a 2x forward P/E discount to the S&P 500, near the widest in 15 years and deeper only in 2017-18 and the 2022 bear market.

Goldman's Delta 1 head noted the SOX trading through the Liberation Day and Iran escalation lows on a blended 24-month basis, with Nvidia at its lowest multiple since 2013, and flagged 2027 as potentially a peak for semis.

Good earnings did not help semis. AMD went from +9% after hours to flat despite data center strength and a >80% revenue growth guide for 2027. Arista faded from +10% to +5% despite a 2027 guide of +38-40% against expectations near 30%.

Oil was the second leg of the rotation. Brent fell about $18 in five days on expectations that a Democratic Congress speeds the end of the Iran war, producing about a 15pt Energy vs Consumer Discretionary spread. Internet names (Expedia, DoorDash, AppLovin) rallied with inverted Brent.

Booking rose 11%, one of its biggest one-day moves in 10+ years, on short positioning of about 20 million shares, a 15+ year low forward EV/EBITDA going into the print, and a Q4 room-night guide of +1-3% seen as a last cut.

Callahan asks whether the market is over-pricing policy outcomes, citing cloud providers over semis, drawdowns in independent power producers and E&Cs, and a sharp consumer discretionary rally. Goldman economists expect data center moratoria to fade in importance and not be long-lived.
Wells Fargo expects the Texas pause to run at least through the end of the legislative session on May 31, 2027, overlapping the year flagged as a possible peak for semis.

The author's call is that capex gets capped and semis de-rate further, because blocked projects only move to Louisiana or Oklahoma eventually. Boova himself does not expect capex numbers to come down soon, which would favor the cheap semis side if he is right.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman's desk sees a clear rotation into hyperscalers. Existing compute capacity becomes scarcer and more valuable, and capex could be capped.
Semis are the source of funds in the rotation, trade at a 2x forward P/E discount to the S&P 500, and face 2027 order risk if data center projects are frozen. The author expects further de-rating.
Brent fell about $18 in five days on expectations of an earlier end to the Iran war. Callahan flags drawdowns in E&Cs and IPPs as part of the policy pricing.
Sharp rally, with Internet names tracking inverted Brent and Booking rising on positioning and valuation.

earnings_insights: AMD reported FQ3 results Nov 4 after the close. Goldman raised its 2027 gross margin estimate to 55.7% and the company guided to >80% revenue growth in 2027 on data center strength offsetting PC weakness. The stock went from +9% after hours to flat.

Arista reported Nov 4 after the close. Revenue growth accelerated into the 50s and the initial 2027 guide is +38-40% against expectations near 30% (consensus estimate per Callahan). The stock faded from +10% to +5% after hours.
Booking reported Nov 4 and guided Q4 room nights +1-3%, seen as a last cut. The stock rose 11% and had traded at a 15+ year low on forward EV/EBITDA going into the print.
Oracle reported 97.9% AI infrastructure utilization with a 20% average renewal/resale premium, per Wells Fargo.
Microsoft had a beat the article calls clean, then raised a $25B bond the next morning. Hyperscalers collectively had negative free cash flow of $31B in Q3, per the author's earlier work.

macro_indicators.interpretation: One of Brent's biggest 5-day declines in recent history, linked by traders to a faster end to the Iran war under a Democratic Congress. It drove a ~15pt Energy vs Consumer Discretionary spread.

trade_ideas.description: Long hyperscalers (cloud providers) versus semis, the rotation pair trade described by Goldman's desk
trade_ideas.rationale: Compute scarcity from a build freeze raises pricing power for installed capacity and may cap capex, while semis are the source of funds.
trade_ideas.risk: Callahan asks whether the market is over-pricing policy outcomes. Boova does not expect capex to come down soon, which would make semis the cheap side.

risk_factors: Policy over-pricing: data center moratoria could fade, as Goldman economists expect, reversing the rotation.
If hyperscaler capex does not fall, the buyback thesis fails and semis at a 2x discount become the cheap side of the trade.
If capex is capped, 2027 chip estimates are too high and the de-rating has further to run.
Hyperscaler free cash flow is negative and bond-funded, so buybacks are not near.
Chip companies carry heavy debt loads and cannot wait out a moratorium.
Oil reversal could unwind the Energy and Consumer Discretionary spread.
charts_described: Callahan's top chart shows semiconductor forward multiples compressing from 28x to 16x over two months, and the bottom chart shows the SOX's ~2x forward P/E discount to the S&P 500 near the widest in 15 years.
Goldman's US Internet basket relative to the S&P is plotted against inverted Brent, which Callahan says explains some of the action.
vol_and_positioning: Booking had about 20 million shares short going into its print, which contributed to the 11% move.
Goldman derivatives specialist Brian Garrett saw seven signs of healing in semis over the weekend as they snapped a 355-day streak, but cautioned that survival of 2026 comes first.
Callahan flags semis as oversold, with several AI names well below their 200-day moving averages.
Nasdaq 100 futures rallied roughly 400bps off overnight lows hit when Texas turned blue.
geopolitical: Democratic election wins, including Texas turning blue, raise the prospect of state-level data center moratoria in Texas, Georgia and Michigan.
Traders priced a Democratic Congress as a faster path to the end of the Iran war, which pushed crude lower.
The article mentions earlier SOX lows during Liberation Day and the Iran escalation.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's economists expect data center moratoria will not be long-lived, while the Wells Fargo note expects the Texas pause to run through May 31, 2027.
Goldman's Boova does not think capex numbers come down anytime soon, which conflicts with the capex-cap premise of the Goldman desk's hyperscaler rotation.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's desk argues a build freeze makes existing compute scarcer and pricier, and lower spending may allow buybacks. Wells Fargo shows H100 rental rates up 26% y/y and Oracle utilization at 97.9%.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscalers burned $31B of free cash flow in Q3 and still borrow, so buybacks are a leap. Boova does not expect capex to fall soon, which would leave semis at a 2x discount as the cheap side.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Capex numbers coming down would hurt semis further, while Goldman economists expect moratoria to fade, which would reverse the rotation.

tension_points.bull_case: Semis trade at about 16x forward earnings, a 2x discount to the S&P 500 and the widest in about 15 years, and the move is called oversold. Goldman economists expect moratoria to be short-lived.
tension_points.bear_case: If Texas, Georgia and Michigan freeze projects, 2027 chip orders tied to them slip first. Even good AMD and Arista prints got faded, and the Delta 1 desk flagged 2027 as potentially a peak.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Texas pause lasting past the May 31, 2027 end of the legislative session would deepen the de-rating, while a short-lived moratorium would support semis.
